mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen monotonically from 9.9 to 9.1 over the four weekly means, meaning a rising share of the population is spending time outside the home. That displaced time converts into non-essential trips, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to fall below 9.1.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility improved 4.6 points in the final week (-32.9 to -28.3), the largest single-week gain in the snapshot. Restored transit ridership proxies restored discretionary trip-making, which lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its trailing 28-day mean within 14 days after a TRANSIT week-on-week gain greater than 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS jumped from -57.6 to -43.4 at t-1w, a 14.2-point outdoor-activity surge. Outdoor recreation substitutes for indoor discretionary browsing, so weeks in which PARKS is elevated coincide with weaker RETAIL_REC over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -45 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: In weeks when PARKS prints above -45, the subsequent 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or higher than the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has deteriorated steadily from -12.0 to -14.6 across the snapshot, showing households are consolidating even essential trips. That trip-consolidation habit suppresses total out-of-home shopping frequency, dragging RETAIL_REC lower over two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds its trailing 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM continues to print at or below -14.6.

mechanism_narrative: The joint signal of rising TRANSIT (-32.9 to -28.3) and falling RESIDENTIAL (9.3 to 9.1) means commuting and out-of-home presence are re-converging. Only when both move together does weekday discretionary footfall rebuild, so RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT gains more than 3 points while RESIDENTIAL falls below 9.5 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days in the weeks where both TRANSIT rose more than 3 points and RESIDENTIAL fell below 9.5.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES improved in three of four weeks (-31.1 to -29.1), consistent with a staged return-to-office mandate. Office repopulation restores lunchtime and after-work retail demand in business districts, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves in two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is below its trailing 28-day mean in more than half of instances where WORKPLACES rose two weeks running.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS retreated 3.9 points from its t-1w peak (-43.4 to -47.3), marking the end of the outdoor-activity pulse. As park visits fade, discretionary spending rotates back indoors, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week of the retracement.
candidate_trigger: PARKS retraces more than 3 points from its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: After a PARKS weekly retracement greater than 3 points, the following 7-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the preceding 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are recovering while GROCERY_PHARM deteriorates to -14.6, a divergence showing mobility is reallocating rather than expanding. Reallocation-funded trips crowd out discretionary spend, so RETAIL_REC mean over four weeks falls below its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 1 point while TRANSIT rises more than 2 points in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds its trailing 28-day mean in weeks where GROCERY_PHARM fell more than 1 point while TRANSIT rose more than 2 points.
